text: As the Patriots prepare to host the Steelers at Gillette Stadium on Sunday, September 20 at 1 PM ET for their home opener, they'll do so without one of their key offensive weapons: wide receiver A.J. Brown, who suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 and has been placed on injured reserve, forcing him to miss at least four games while the team figures out who steps up in his absence. Drake Maye and Head Coach Mike Vrabel will need to navigate this significant blow to the passing game, though the rookie quarterback has shown his character off the field this week, joining his wife Ann Michael in surprising teachers at Alfred Lima Sr. Elementary School in Providence by funding the Amazon classroom wish lists of more than 50 educators. The organization also made headlines for a different reason when Robert Kraft had rapper Macklemore removed as an opening act for Ed Sheeran's upcoming shows at Gillette Stadium, citing his "history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community." With injury reports to monitor and the challenge of bouncing back after Week 1, the Patriots will look to get right against Pittsburgh while managing both on-field adversity and the team's off-field values.
